newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Norilsk's Dudinka ice begins breaking up.
newsitem.headline: Russian Norilsk's Dudinka ice begins breaking up.

text.p: Ice has started breaking up at the main export outlet for Russia's Norilsk Nickel, and vessels will start loading metals from Norilsk's northern port of Dudinka on June 15-18, a company spokesman said.
He gave no details for planned export volumes of nickel, cobalt and other metals.

A late winter last year meant that ice began breaking up at Dudinka only in the first week of June. Dudinka, on the Yenisei River near Norilsk, is ice-bound for much of the year and usually operates for 100-120 days a year.
Norilsk is one of the world's largest nickel producers and is the largest producer of platinum group metals in Russia, which is the world's largest palladium and second biggest platinum supplier.
